newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: GOVT TOLD TO BE PROACTIVE IN INDUSTRY AFTER BHP DECISION

A former Manager of the Newcastle Steelworks says the Federal Government must urgently formulate a proactive industry policy, following the decision to close the plant in two years. Rob Chenery, who spent two years in the job, says BHP is now investing in steelmaking in Asia, because that will satisfy shareholder demands for higher returns within the company's steel division.
The company announced yesterday, it would close the aging Newcastle plant, claiming it is no longer internationally competitive.
Mr Chenery told ABC Radio the steelworks needed a major re-investment, and the Federal Government has a key role in attracting investment to the manufacturing industry.
ACTU TARGETS GOVT OVER BHP CLOSURE
ACTU President, Jenny George, says steel unions are likely to meet in Newcastle later this week to plan a campaign against the closure of BHP's steelworks.
Ms George says BHP has betrayed the commitment of steel workers and the Newcastle community to keeping the plant operating.
But she says the lack of a workable national industry policy means the Federal Government must also bear some responsibility for the closure.
HANSON WON'T SELL OUT BELIEF FOR TRADE
Federal Independent MP Pauline Hanson says beliefs should not be sold out to maintain business trade.
Former Northern Territory chief minister and now honorary Malaysian consul, Paul Everingham, says Ms Hanson's comments on Asia are threatening trade.
Mr Everingham says support for Ms Hanson's One Nation party could produce a recession.
But Ms Hanson says she stands by her comments and criticism of them by other politicians is a scare tactic.
She says Australia used to have four per cent of world trade, but it fell to one percent, long before she was heard of. - - - -
FAMILY OF MURDERED TEEN UNHAPPY ABOUT FILM
The solicitor representing the family of murdered Newcastle teenager, Leigh Leigh, says a film based on the murder glosses over the brutality of the crime.
The promoters of Blackrock deny their story of the rape and murder of a 15-year-old at a beach party is the actual story of what happened to Leigh, who died in similar circumstances in 1989.
However solicitor John Boersig, says the film features a murder scene which doesn't convey the agonising and drawn out death which Leigh suffered.
Mr Boersig told ABC Radio because the film is loosely based on real events, it should have portrayed them as accurately as possible.
SOUTH AFRICA SAYS OLYMPICS SHOULD NOT BE BOYCOTTED LIGHTLY
The South African Government says boycott of the Sydney Olympics should not be taken up lightly.
Rejecting the Prime Minister, John Howard's plan on native title, Indigenous leaders say they'll lobby African nations to boycott the Sydney Olympics.
South Africa's Trade Minister, Alec Erwin, says until the current dispute over native title in Australia becomes multi-lateral, it should be left to Australia to resolve.
Mr Erwin says South Africa would like to see a balance between events which unify nations like the Olympics, and justice within nations.
The Minister offered to assist Australia saying South Africa would be happy to share its experience in the struggle against racism.
But Mr Erwin says the Olympics are the unification of sporting nations and should not be boycotted lightly.
DEAD YOUTH'S BODY REMAINS UNIDENTIFIED
A post-mortem examination's being carried out this afternoon on the body of a young man, found earlier today on Sydney's north shore.
A passer-by found the body at about six-thirty, lying on a nature strip in the suburb of Gordon.
Police say he was wounded in the back of the head.
They've been unable to identify him, but believe he was aged between 16 and 20 years old.
NEW CHIEF FOR FEDERAL LIBERAL PARTY
The Federal Liberal Party has announced that Andrew Robb's deputy, Lynton Crosby, will take over as the party's Federal Director.
Mr Robb resigned last week after seven years in the top job.
Mr Crosby has served as deputy since 1994, and has been active in politics for 20 years.
His CV includes stints as an advisor to parliamentarians, Vice President of the South Australian Liberal Party, and State Director of the Queensland division of the party.
Mr Crosby has been unanimously backed by the party's Federal Executive, after a telephone hook-up today.
HOWARD LAUNCHES CHARITY IN MEMORY OF PORT ARTHUR VICTIMS
The Prime Minister says a charity he launched today in memory of two young victims of the Port Arthur massacre will provide much needed help and support for child victims of violent crime.
The Alannah and Madeline foundation, has been set up by Walter Mikac whose daughters were killed at Port Arthur.
Mr Howard says the foundation has a simple aspiration, to recognise the need for love, compassion and support of children who are victims of crime and violence in the community.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
